title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A licence plate camera network built to support police work was queried by an officer against a person he had a personal history with, and the same officer is said to have used separate state systems for the same purpose. The misuse happened at the point of use, by an authorised operator with legitimate credentials, which is the hardest place for a technical control to intervene.

The facts describe repeated searches across two years rather than a single query, and they describe a target who had deliberately changed her identity, phone number and social habits. Catching this would have required auditing who queried whom and why, and comparing that pattern against the officer's own connections. Nothing in the reporting says such an audit existed or that any system flagged the searches before the woman found out.

What is established is an accusation, a criminal complaint filed by the department, and administrative leave. Whether Rogers did what he is accused of, and what he intended, is not established by these reports.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of misusing police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location using the Flock camera system multiple times in 2024 and 2025. The department also said he used state systems to obtain information about her.

Stow police filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and placed him on paid leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order against him for at least a year. The police chief said a Select Board hearing will be held next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
